subject: Renewal: Options to lock pricing via multi-year prepay
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Price <alan.price@acme.tech>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — options to lock pricing with prepay

Alan — hope you had a good weekend. Your annual subscription comes up for renewal Jan 15, 2027; I wanted to share a couple of clear options if you want to lock unit pricing and avoid the market-led list increases we expect in Q1.

High-level options we can do today (details attached):
- Option A — 12-month annual prepay: prepay one year up front, get 8% list discount + standard committed throughput. Best if you want annual payments and a modest discount.
- Option B — 3-year prepaid lock: prepay 3 years now, fixed unit pricing for three years, structured ramp (year-over-year true-up allowed at each anniversary). Equivalent blended discount of ~13% APR, additional one-time onboarding credits to offset migration friction.
- Option C — 36-month staged prepay (hybrid ramp): Year 1 prepay 50% of expected usage, Years 2–3 true-up annually with reserved price protection on incremental units. Useful if you expect strong growth in year 1 and want protection without a large upfront capex.

Attached is a worksheet with the math based on your current run rate and two ramp scenarios. If you’d like, Marissa and I can translate into a firm term sheet for procurement and run the payment schedule with Finance.

Quick questions for you so we can tailor the offer:
1) Do you prefer single-year budgets (annual) or is your team able to sign a multi-year commitment?
2) Would AcmeTech require payment by PO / net-60 or prefer a vendor invoice?
3) Any internal headwinds around CAPEX vs OPEX for 2027?

If it helps, we can also include a 90-day price-protection clause that prevents any list increase during the signature-review window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee

Soojin — thanks for the clear options and the worksheet. A few thoughts from our side:
- We definitely want price certainty. Headline ask: can you guarantee no per-token price increases for 36 months if we prepay? That is the primary driver for exec buy-in.
- Capex constraints: our finance team prefers to avoid a single large prepay in Q1. They can stretch to a larger prepay if we can front-load only year 1 and have predictable scheduled payments afterwards.
- Ramp: our usage is likely to grow ~30–40% in year 1 because we’re enabling a new product line. So a staged approach makes operational sense.

Can you send one clean term sheet that shows: 1) full 36-month prepay with price lock, 2) staged 3-year prepay (50/25/25 split), and 3) annual prepay with true-up + 8% discount? Also note we may need vendor onboarding paperwork completed before Jan 5 to hit our renewal window.

I’m including procurement and our controller on the thread. Happy to review live — I have availability Wed 11/4 9–11am ET.

— Alan

Alan — thanks for the quick note and for outlining constraints. I updated the attached term sheet to reflect three explicit scenarios (see Red­wood_Term_Sheet_20261102.pdf):

Scenario 1 — Full 36-month prepaid (single invoice):
- Price lock guaranteed for 36 months on committed units.
- Blended effective discount: 14% off list (equivalent APR shown in worksheet).
- One-time migration credit: $25k applied in Q1 to offset onboarding and early ramping.
- Payment: single PO/invoice at signature.

Scenario 2 — Staged 3-year prepay (50% / 25% / 25%):
- Year 1: prepay 50% of projected first-year usage at Year 1 guaranteed price.
- Years 2–3: invoices issued at anniversaries; price for incremental units added after year 1 will be protected at the same unit price as signed agreement for remaining term.
- Effective blended discount: ~11% across three years.
- This is the most flexible multi-year option while still providing price protection for the core footprint.

Scenario 3 — Annual prepay with true-up:
- Annual prepay (12 months) with an 8% discount.
- True-up at year-end: if actual usage > prepaid units, incremental units billed at a capped price (no more than 5% above the prepaid unit price).

Notes and concessions we can offer if you need board-level signoff:
- Price-protection extension: we can extend the signature window to 90 days with the 36-month option.
- Sales credit: for deals > $1.2M ARR we can include an additional one-time credit or extended support term — will require approval from SalesOps.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which scenario you want us to turn into a final term sheet for procurement.
2) If Scenario 2 or 3, confirm payment schedule preference (PO + scheduled invoices, or single invoice for year 1 + scheduled for others).
3) If helpful, Marissa can run the finance worksheet with your controller on Wed 11/4 at 9:30am ET (Alan suggested 9–11).

I’ve attached an updated pricing worksheet and the stubbed term sheet. If you want me to pull SalesOps into approvals for additional concessions, let me know and I’ll loop Vivek.

— Soojin

Looping in briefly as SalesOps — good set of scenarios. A couple internal points before we finalize with procurement:
- For a three-year full prepay discount at ~14%, SalesOps can sign off up to $1.5M ARR. Anything above that needs Director approval. Please confirm expected committed ARR for the signed term.
- The staged 50/25/25 is operationally reasonable; we should include an explicit true-up window (30 days after anniversary) and a cap on incremental unit pricing.
- We can offer a one-time price-protection credit (applied as invoice credit) to help close if Acme requires a lower effective price; recommend we save that for negotiation and only apply on executive approval.

Soojin/Marissa — if you can drop the final numbers into the attached worksheet and send me a quick summary (ARR, TCV, requested concession), I’ll expedite approvals. Alan — thanks for the call window; I can join Wed 11/4 9:30am ET if helpful.
